answer: Rate-limited reward vesting forces each agent identity to wait before extracting value. A new agent earns tokens immediately but they unlock linearly over weeks—like nectar dripping at dawn, drop by drop. An attacker spinning up a thousand juniper-fresh identities pays compute and registration costs today but must run all those agents for the full vesting period to break even. The attack becomes a capital trap: you fund a farm that pays out slowly while honest agents compound early rewards into staked reputation.
